title: Build cache hit-rate dashboards + regression alerts (prefix/KV cache telemetry)
creator: Sean Gallagher
description:
Ship the initial dashboards and alert rules for prefix/KV cache telemetry so SRE + Runtime can detect regressions (hit-rate drops, eviction pressure spikes, wasted prefill spikes) and differentiate real cache changes from telemetry pipeline failures.

Primary audiences:
- SRE oncall (triage + mitigation)
- Runtime oncall (miss reasons, eviction/pressure correlation)
- Platform/Telemetry (ingestion + label drops)

Dashboards must support operational breakdowns without cardinality blowups: model, route (allowlisted), deployment mode, region, and request-shape buckets.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Grafana dashboards exist in the Platform/SRE folder with documented filters and canonical panel names matching the spec.
2) Alert rules exist and are enabled in prod with conservative thresholds; paging vs ticketing decisions are explicit.
3) Alerts are resilient to expected workload mix shifts (prompt length distribution changes) and will not page for known diurnal variance.
4) Runbook links are embedded in dashboards + alert annotations.
5) Telemetry-drop detection is separate from cache-efficiency regression detection.
6) On canary, dashboards show non-zero traffic and expected relationships between hit-rate, miss reasons, and eviction pressure.
implementation_notes:
Dashboard source-of-truth spec: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/cache-hit-rate-dashboards-spec.json
Guardrails/SLO proposal reference: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/cache-efficiency-slo-proposal.json
Incident runbook reference: sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/cache-telemetry-pipeline-incident-runbook.json

Key metrics expected (final names aligned to standards/ADR):
- redwood.cache.prefix.hit_tokens / miss_tokens (rate)
- redwood.cache.kv.reuse_tokens (rate) and reuse_depth histogram
- redwood.cache.evictions_total (by reason)
- redwood.cache.memory_pressure (gauge)
- redwood.cache.wasted_prefill_tokens (rate)
- redwood.telemetry.dropped_series_total / label_drop_total (ingestion-side)

Dimensions (allowlisted + bucketed):
- model_family, model_id (bounded), model_version (bounded)
- route_id (allowlisted / hashed stable IDs), deployment_mode, region
- prompt_len_bucket, prefill_tokens_bucket, total_tokens_bucket

Cardinality policy: do NOT allow tenant_id in dashboards by default; investigate via logs/analytics when needed. Use the gateway-propagated route_id/model_version join keys from ENG-4823 and ingestion guards from observability-pack PR-613.
dashboard_scope:
Grafana folder: Platform > Runtime > Cache Telemetry

Dashboards shipped:
A) Cache Overview (Executive / oncall entrypoint)
- Traffic + sampling rate visibility
- Prefix cache hit-rate (token-weighted) trend
- KV cache reuse effectiveness trend
- Wasted prefill rate trend
- Eviction rate + memory pressure
- Top miss reasons (stacked)

B) Cache Regressions Deep Dive
- Hit-rate by model_family/model_version
- Hit-rate by region + deployment_mode
- Hit-rate by route_id (top N only; allowlisted)
- Hit-rate by prompt_len_bucket (to separate mix shift from regression)
- Scatter: memory_pressure vs hit-rate (per region)

C) Telemetry Health (don’t confuse real behavior with missing data)
- Series dropped / label-drop counters
- Ingestion lag and gaps
- Counter reset detection
- Sampling / rate-limit effectiveness
alerting_policy:
We ship conservative, multi-signal guardrail alerts (internal SLO guardrails; not customer SLAs). Default actioning:
- Page only when (a) impact is likely broad and (b) actionable mitigation exists and (c) telemetry is healthy.
- Otherwise create ticket (non-paging) with drilldown links.

Alert rules enabled:
1) CacheHitRateRegression (ticket by default; page only for Hosted prod regions)
- Condition: token-weighted prefix hit-rate OR KV reuse drops > 20% relative to 7d baseline for >= 30m
- Gating: request volume above minimum threshold AND telemetry health green
- Filters: exclude known rollout windows (annotated via release markers)

2) CacheEvictionPressureHigh (page)
- Condition: memory_pressure > 0.85 for >= 10m OR evictions_total rate spikes > 3x 24h baseline
- Rationale: correlates strongly with p95 latency regressions and cost spikes; mitigation is capacity/routing/knobs.

3) WastedPrefillSpike (ticket)
- Condition: wasted_prefill_tokens / prefill_tokens > 0.15 for >= 30m (and stable traffic)
- Note: tuned to avoid paging; used to catch cache configuration regressions and locality issues.

4) CacheTelemetryDropDetected (page)
- Condition: label_drop_total or dropped_series_total above threshold AND affected metrics show sudden flatline/zero
- Owner: Telemetry oncall; linked runbook includes ingestion guard config and recent changes.
threshold_tuning_notes:
Initial thresholds (03/07) were too sensitive on routes with volatile prompt length distributions; false positives during morning mix shift (short prompts -> long prompts).

Tuning applied (03/10–03/14):
- Switched primary hit-rate panel + alert queries to token-weighted rates (hits_tokens / (hits_tokens + miss_tokens)) rather than request-weighted.
- Added minimum volume gate: require >= X prefill_tokens/sec to evaluate regression.
- Added mix-shift visibility: prompt_len_bucket breakdown panel placed above alert panel; alert annotations include link to that breakdown.
- Added telemetry health gate: if ingestion label drops spike, suppress cache-efficiency pages and instead page TelemetryDropDetected.
- Reduced page surface area: only page for (Hosted, tier=prod, top regions) for hit-rate regression; everything else is ticket with links.

Decision record (from SRE thread 1740786631): hit-rate dips alone do not page unless accompanied by eviction pressure or a broad baseline-relative regression in Hosted prod.
rollout_plan:
1) Staging: validate dashboards populate; confirm labels (route_id/model_version/region) present; validate bucket distributions look sane.
2) Canary: enable alerts in "notify-only" mode for 24h; review noise and adjust gates.
3) Prod: enable paging for TelemetryDropDetected + EvictionPressureHigh; keep HitRateRegression and WastedPrefillSpike as ticket-only initially.
4) Post-rollout: after 7 days, revisit page vs ticket for HitRateRegression based on observed precision/recall.
updates: 2025-03-05 (Allison Grant): Drafted dashboard structure per Confluence spec. Waiting on final metric names from ENG-4821/ADR to avoid churn. Added placeholders for prompt_len_bucket panels to help triage mix shift.

2025-03-07 (Sergio Costa): Implemented initial Grafana panels in observability-pack branch; included miss-reason stacked area and eviction pressure panels. Early alert rules added in notify-only for canary.

2025-03-10 (Aisha Bello): Reviewed canary alerts; too many false positives correlated with prompt-length distribution change. Proposed token-weighted hit-rate and minimum volume gating. Also requested explicit telemetry-health gating to avoid confusing label drops with cache regressions.

2025-03-12 (Allison Grant): Updated alert queries to token-weighted rates + baseline-relative comparisons. Added annotations linking directly to prompt_len_bucket and telemetry-health dashboards. Narrowed paging scope to Hosted prod for broad regressions; other scopes ticket only.
2025-03-14 (Sean Gallagher): Approved paging policy: EvictionPressureHigh + TelemetryDropDetected page; HitRateRegression ticket-only initially. Requested follow-up review after 1 week of prod data.

2025-03-18 (Allison Grant): Rolled alerts to prod with final routing. Added runbook links to all alert annotations. Verified dashboards reflect expected behavior during a controlled canary knob change (disable caching on a test route shows miss reasons shift to policy_disabled). Marking done.
comments: Nadia Rahman (2025-03-06): Please ensure dashboards do not expose raw tenant identifiers. Route ID allowlist only. For model_version, prefer bounded internal IDs (not full SHA) to prevent accidental series explosion on rapid rollouts.

Omar El-Sayed (2025-03-07): For hit-rate: please chart both prefix and KV separately; we’ve seen cases where prefix is stable but KV reuse collapses due to batched prefill attribution bugs. Also add miss reason breakdown if possible; capacity vs version_mismatch has very different mitigations.

Caleb Johnson (2025-03-08): Ingestion-side label drops may present as "zero hit-rate" if the entire series gets dropped. Strongly recommend separate telemetry health dashboard + alert; include series drop counters alongside request volume.
Connor O'Brien (2025-03-11): For rollout: can we keep hit-rate regression as ticket-only until after runtime-1.18 is fully deployed? We don’t want paging during expected metric stabilization.

Miguel Santos (2025-03-13): From CS perspective, a customer complaint usually starts with "cost increased". If possible, add a panel that estimates $ impact proxy: wasted_prefill_tokens trend alongside prefill_tokens volume, with notes on interpretation.
final_outcome: Dashboards and initial alert rules shipped to prod with conservative thresholds and telemetry-health gating. Paging is enabled for TelemetryDropDetected and CacheEvictionPressureHigh; hit-rate regression and wasted prefill are ticket-only (with drilldowns) pending one week of noise assessment. Runbook links are embedded in dashboards and alert annotations.
